title: Vehicle Build Cost Calculator
shortSummary: Owner-scoped build budgets with planned, actual and projected costs across independent scenarios.
problem: Build estimates need explicit prices, consistent scenario links and a reliable ownership boundary.
architecture: React communicates with an ASP.NET Core API; EF Core persists owner-scoped records and decimal costs in PostgreSQL.
decisions: Scope queries and summaries to the JWT owner, including parent links.
Keep unknown legacy costs and owners unassigned; never infer money from notes.
Compare alternatives separately and include shared costs once.
highlights: Build and scenario CRUD with linked parts, labor and forecast allowances.
Server-calculated planned, actual and projected totals; EUR, USD and GBP without conversion.
outcome: 38 backend tests, frontend build, real browser cost edits and PostgreSQL migration/persistence checks passed.
constraints: Full line totals only: no quantity pricing, partial-payment ledger, receipts or currency conversion.
Production secrets, token lifecycle, deployment migrations and broader accessibility review remain.

title: Flowchart-to-Code
shortSummary: A visual editor that validates structured graphs and generates pseudocode, Python and JavaScript.
problem: Branch joins and invalid graph connections can silently change the meaning of generated code.
architecture: React Flow sends a graph to Express; validation precedes a shared intermediate representation and three language renderers.
decisions: Validate connectivity and outgoing edges after adjacency construction.
Use common postdominators to identify shared continuations.
Clear stale output after edits and discard delayed responses.
highlights: Edit nodes and connections, reset examples, copy and download generated source.
Actionable feedback for invalid graphs and unsupported structures.
outcome: 36 backend tests with Python enabled, two frontend API tests, HTTP checks and real browser workflows passed.
constraints: Acyclic sequences and structured decisions only; loops and crossing overlaps are rejected.
Labels are emitted as verbatim code: no expression parser, type checker or safe-code guarantee.
No diagram persistence or hosted execution. The canvas is designed for desktop/laptop use.

title: MiniLang Interpreter
shortSummary: A TypeScript language pipeline with lexical environments, recursion, closures and a bounded browser playground.
problem: Language features need consistent scope, logical precedence, return behavior and readable execution errors.
architecture: A lexer feeds a recursive-descent parser and tree-walk interpreter. The browser runs the actual interpreter in a disposable worker; the CLI provides a persistent REPL.
decisions: Give blocks child environments and separate AND/OR precedence.
Validate native arity/types and propagate returns explicitly.
Bound visits, call depth and output; terminate browser workers on timeout.
highlights: Inspect editable examples including factorial and returned counter closures.
Display tokens/statement counts, output and language errors; preserve/reset REPL state.
outcome: 62 interpreter tests, type checks, CLI/REPL checks, production build and browser examples passed.
constraints: Educational language: no arrays/objects, modules or JavaScript interop; numbers use JavaScript floating-point behavior.
Worker limits are demo safeguards, not a hardened hostile-code sandbox or memory quota.
Manual Stop was not independently confirmed; interpreter-budget termination and subsequent recovery were verified.

title: TaskFlow
shortSummary: A task manager with browser-local storage or an optional file-backed Express API.
problem: Tasks should survive normal restarts and failed loads should be recoverable without losing edit feedback.
architecture: A React task hook uses interchangeable storage adapters. The Express demo validates records and replaces JSON snapshots before publishing mutations in memory.
decisions: Keep components independent of the selected storage adapter.
Clear completed tasks through one atomic server operation.
Add Retry loading and visible edit errors that retain the draft.
highlights: Add, edit, complete, reopen and delete tasks; filter active/completed items.
Separate local/API lists, retained theme and responsive inline editing.
outcome: 29 client tests, 16 server tests, both production builds and browser/restart checks passed; package audits reported zero at preparation time.
constraints: No accounts, authentication, automatic synchronization or hosted database guarantees.
Snapshot persistence supports one process and small lists; no power-loss guarantee or concurrent-edit protection.
Browser and API modes keep separate lists. Hosted durability and physical-device coverage remain unverified.

title: Sfera Tag Scanner
shortSummary: A Kotlin Android inventory app with a synthetic-input browser companion powered by shared reference, quantity and duplicate rules.
problem: Clothing-tag references must preserve leading zeros, distinguish exact duplicates from color variants and reject invalid stock operations.
architecture: The Android source uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt and Room, with CameraX and ML Kit image-input paths and basic Apache POI spreadsheet helpers. The separate browser companion calls a loopback Kotlin HTTP server compiling the actual InventoryRules.kt and SferaCode.kt. Its inventory and movement adapter is server-side and in memory; it does not run Room or reproduce the Android interface.
decisions: Share platform-independent Kotlin reference, quantity and duplicate rules with Android rather than reimplementing them in JavaScript.
Correct status filtering, reject malformed references, invalid quantities, duplicate entries and repeated exits.
Make unfinished Bluetooth/USB/NFC RFID adapters explicitly report unsupported instead of claiming a successful connection.
Keep the companion synthetic and loopback-only, with a bounded 128 MB Java heap and no API credentials.
highlights: Inspect a dotted reference while retaining leading zeros; distinguish a color variant from an exact duplicate.
Companion inventory supports synthetic entry, full-reference exit, movement history, search and status filtering.
Restore the Gradle wrapper and remove generated Android build products from Git tracking; update the basic spreadsheet dependency without claiming native compatibility verification.
outcome: Preparation passed 18 actual Kotlin core assertions and real Chromium workflow/mobile checks. Integration verifies the running companion without resetting existing inventory. Native Gradle configuration reached SDK discovery and stopped because the Android SDK is missing.
constraints: Native Android build remains blocked by the missing SDK. Camera capture, physical OCR, optional remote image extraction, Room persistence and device file access were not verified.
RFID is unfinished: no tested reader connection, EPC mapping or hardware compatibility is claimed.
Companion inventory/history are server-side in memory, not browser storage. State resets on server restart or explicit sample reset; there is no authentication or persistence.
Exit marks the entire reference out, not a partial sale. Native save/movement transactions and failure recovery still need integration tests.
Spreadsheet helpers read the first worksheet/seven fields and create a new workbook; they do not preserve macros, quantities/status/history or provide full inventory sync/backup.
No affiliation, commissioning, individual contribution narrative, production deployment or business outcome is inferred.

title: Smart Gym Transformation App
shortSummary: Log workouts and body measurements, then review dated training progress and weight trends.
architecture: A React and TypeScript interface shares record editors and an API client. Demo mode uses browser storage with fictional records. The ASP.NET Core API uses EF Core and PostgreSQL with account-scoped queries and rotating refresh cookies.
problem: Connect dated workout sessions and body measurements to a readable progress history.
decisions: Store workout dates independently from record creation timestamps.
Store duration in whole minutes and weight in kilograms, with a display unit switch.
Keep older records with unknown ownership excluded from authenticated account views.
highlights: Create and edit a workout, then filter its history by date.
Log body weight and switch the progress display between kilograms and pounds.
Reset fictional demo records or use the documented full-stack setup.
constraints: The browser demo uses fictional data saved to the current browser. It does not connect to the account API.
Full-stack use requires the documented PostgreSQL and API setup and private server signing configuration.
The handoff records an older development signing key in repository history. Public deployment requires resolving that historical exposure.
outcome: The source handoff records seven backend tests, Release and frontend builds, lint, TypeScript, browser workflows and PostgreSQL integration checks including account isolation and token rotation. Changes remain local.
